examples.solution_text:
Find the cross-sectional area using the parallel sides and perpendicular depth.
$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{0.8(2+1.2)}{2}\\&=1.28\text{ m}^2\\V&=Ah\\&=1.28\times5\\&=6.4\text{ m}^3\end{align*}$
Convert the volume to litres.
$\begin{align*}C&=6.4\times1000\\&=6400\text{ L}\end{align*}$
Divide the capacity by the filling rate.
$\begin{align*}t&=\frac{6400}{200}\\&=32\text{ minutes}\end{align*}$

Subtract the notch area from the full rectangle area, then multiply by the prism length.
$\begin{align*}A&=(9\times7)-(3\times2)\\&=63-6\\&=57\text{ cm}^2\\V&=Ah\\&=57\times8\\&=456\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$

Find the rectangle and trapezium areas separately, then add them.
$\begin{align*}A_1&=10\times5\\&=50\text{ mm}^2\\A_2&=\frac{9(10+18)}{2}\\&=126\text{ mm}^2\\A&=50+126\\&=176\text{ mm}^2\\V&=Ah\\&=176\times20\\&=3520\text{ mm}^3\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Upper rectangle height = 6−2 = 4 cm. Cross-sectional area = 8×2 + 3×4 = 28 cm². Volume = 28×9 = 252 cm³. Matches the rectangular dissection taught in Volume A guided practice (a).

Triangle height = 5−2 = 3 m. Rectangle area = 14 m²; triangle area = 7×3÷2 = 10.5 m². Volume = (14+10.5)×4 = 98 m³. The cross-section adapts Volume A Foundation 2(e) with a rectangle-and-triangle dissection.

Trapezium area = 0.8×(2+1.2)÷2 = 1.28 m². Volume = 1.28×5 = 6.4 m³; capacity = 6400 L; filling time = 6400÷200 = 32 minutes. Combines the capacity method in Development 6 with the filling-time method in Mastery 11.

Enclosing rectangle area = 9×7 = 63 cm². Notch area = 3×2 = 6 cm². Remaining area = 57 cm²; volume = 57×8 = 456 cm³. Rectangular removal applies the supplied subtraction teaching and preserves the accepted assessed method.

Rectangle area = 10×5 = 50 mm². Trapezium area = 9×(10+18)÷2 = 126 mm². Total area = 176 mm²; volume = 176×20 = 3520 mm³. Diagram and dissection match the composite cross-section in Volume A Development 7.
Sloping section length = 26−8 = 18 m. Deep rectangle area = 8×3 = 24 m². Sloping trapezium area = 18×(3+1.5)÷2 = 40.5 m². Excavation volume = (24+40.5)×9 = 580.5 m³. Matches Volume A Mastery 9.
With the uniform cross-sectional area supplied, V = Ah = 0.32×7.5 = 2.4 m³. Matches Volume A Review 1(d); a diagram is unnecessary because both required quantities are explicit.
